hard_case: the first assertion cannot see the dropped field, but a second assertion on a fresh input pins `ok`

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.failing_test: marked settings keep the input and set ok
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: changes the value the changed line returns

reasoning: `return { ...cfg, ok: true }` becomes `return { ...cfg }`. The `toEqual(cfg)` assertion passes on both versions, but `markBoth({ name: "bo" }).ok` reads `undefined` after the edit and fails `toBe(true)`. RIPR-SPEC-0246 example 14 (the second-assertion form) reads this `exposed`.
